title: Deliver task-linked context in prompt hooks for one explicit file
context: Existing hook guidance asked agents to request hunch_context even when the prompt named a concrete repository file. Touches invariant(s): con_03a0b94b2e (The agent hook must never block an edit on failure: any error exits 0 and never denies; after the event is recognized it emits at most one 'grounding unavailable' context line, unrecognized input emits nothing); con_8460b6770f (Config/provider writers must merge idempotently into existing user files and refuse to clobber an unparseable file); con_e04226bd05 (The MCP server must stay client-agnostic: all assistants point to the same .hunch/ graph; no Claude-only behavior in the server).
decision: Allow UserPromptSubmit hooks to supply first context for one validated, explicitly named file when native session and task linkage are available. Retain the hunch_context route when the brief cannot be supplied.
consequences: Agents can use the brief for its covered file; other edit scopes still require constraint checks.
Target selection rejects sensitive paths, symlinks, and files outside the repository, and canonicalizes accepted paths.
Passive delivery is skipped for checkouts advertising team memory unless an explicit private overlay is configured.
Target resolution does not retain task prose.
alternatives_rejected: Require a separate hunch_context call even when a task-linked prompt brief covers the file.
Treat public-only hook memory as sufficient for a checkout advertising team memory.
